To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we have prepared and fully characterized a series of amphiphilicsugar-modified guanosines, which are able to form G-quadrupleges, and that some of them are good low-molecularweight organogelators, and are able to transport H(+) across lipid membranes.
a series of guanosine derivatives have been designed, prepared and fully characterised, with particular focus on their ability to meditate H(+) transport through lipid bilayers.

a small series of guanosine derivatives was designed, synthesized and fully characterized, showing that they are able to form G-tetrad and G-quadrupelx structures, to act as ion carriers, and to exhibit a significant cytotoxicity against human MCF7 cells.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the preparation of a series of sugar-modified nucleosides, which are endowed with interesting properties, including self-assembly in solution, ion transportation and cytotoxicity, and which could be used as building blocks for the construction of more complex systems.

the design, synthesis, characterisation, self-assembly and biological evaluation of a series of sugar-modified nucleobases, which may be considered a new class of amphiphiles, endowed with peculiar biological properties.
the synthesis of a small library of guanosine derivatives bearing different hydrophilic and hydrophobic groups.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the insertion of hydrophilic groups into guanosine-based molecules can lead to compounds with a wide range of biological properties, such as ion transportation and cytotoxic activity, which are potentially useful in biotechnology and medicine.

the sugar moiety is a key factor in the formation of G-tetrads and G-quadruplices, while the presence of a hydrophilic group is essential for the ability to form gels, to act as a transporter and to be cytotoxic.

the structural modifications introduced on the sugar moiety of guanosine derivatives, as well as the introduction of hydrophilic groups and/or charged functional groups, may influence the formation of G-tetrads, G-quadrupexes and G-quadruploxides, as well as ion transportation and cytotoxicity.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

guanosine-based derivatives can be designed to form G-quadruplices in solution and to self-assemble in organic solvents, and that they can also mediate ion transportation and exert cytotoxic activity.

the introduction of a sugar moiety in the guanosine molecule, in combination with the presence of a hydrophobic chain and/or a positive charge, may provide a suitable molecular architecture for a potential therapeutic application, in particular in cancer treatment.

the introduction of a sugar moiety on a guanine nucleobase, in the presence of an appropriate amphiphilic chain, is an effective strategy to obtain compounds that can be used as low-molecular-weight gels and as potential ion transporters.
The main takeaway from our work is that

guanosine derivatives with a hydrophilic chain, such as an amino acid or an oligoethylene oxide, connected through an in vivo reversible esterase-cleavable ester linkage, may be good candidates for the development of new anticancer drugs.

sugar-modified guanine derivatives, with a suitable balance between hydrophilic and hydrophobic groups, can be considered as a novel class of potential drug candidates, with interesting features for the development of new therapeutic agents for anticancer and antimicrobial treatments.
sugar-modification of guanosine is a powerful tool to generate a variety of G-quadrupleg-forming molecules with interesting biological properties.
